JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 31.12.2023 at about 4.30 p.m, the deceased was going to his village Nangali from Kolar by riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.no.KA-07-EG-6207, along with his wife and two minor sons on the pillion seat, slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations on the correct side of the road.

On the way when they reached near Ajjapanahalli Gate, Kolar - Mulabagal NH-75 road, Kolar Taluk and District, one Maruthi Ertiga car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MF- 7728 came from same direction, driven by its driver at high speed in rash and negligent manner and while taking a U turn, he lost control over his vehicle, went its wrong side of the road and dashed violently against the deceased's motorcycle from behind.
Due to the tremendous impact the deceased fell down along with his motorcycle and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to RL Jalappa hospital, and then to Varalakshmi Hospital, Bengaluru.
On the next day he was shifted to Venkateshwara Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and discharged on 03.01.2024.
On the same day he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, wherein during the course of treatment he succumed the said injuries on 05.01.2024 at about 3.00 p.m.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.

It is submitted that because of untimely death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered economically as well as emotionally and due to unexpected death of deceased, they have undergone mental agony and shock and lost bread earning member of the family.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending car and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, they pray to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.

This respondent has denied that the accident was occurred Shwetha K vs Kartikey Kumar Shukla on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127269412/
2 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.

sentences.text: Further stated that he was following all the traffic rules and regulations of the road safety and with high care he was waiting to take the U turn, and it is only the deceased who came with high speed with rash and negligent manner and dashed to the back side of the respondent No.1 car and sustained injuries.

Infact the accident occurred due to the sole negligence & reckless driving of the deceased himself he was without maintaining the safe distance between the vehicles and without having proper lookout the vehicular movements of the road in carelessly and in the process he lost control and hit the stationed vehicle from behind and caused the accident.
In fact deceased was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident.
The respondent No.1 admitted that he is the RC owner of the Car and was duly insured with the 2nd respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
It is further submitted that the driver of the car also possess valid and effective driving licence.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Without prejudice, it is further contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of insured vehicle.

Infact the accident occurred due to the sole negligence & reckless driving of the deceased himself he was without maintaining the safe distance between the vehicles and without having proper lookout the vehicular movements of the road in carelessly and in the process he lost control and hit the stationed vehicle from behind and caused the accident.
Further the deceased was riding his motorcycle that too without wearing a helmet and without possessing DL.
As such the the deceased himself was responsible for the accident and who is the tortfeasor for his own negligence.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6), 147 and 149 of MV Act is pleaded.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.

On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured,
the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Rest of the petition averments are contended as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 31.12.2023 at about 4.30 p.m.,
near Ajjappanahalli gate U turn, NH-75 road, Kolar - Mulabagal road, Kolar Taluk, Kolar District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of the Maruti Ertiga car bearing Reg.No.KA-53- Shwetha K vs Kartikey Kumar Shukla on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127269412/
3 MF-7728 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 16 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the car himself examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 4 documents.
7. Heard arguments of both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record and arguments.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.2 : The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

Perusal of the evidence on record makes it evident that deceased was riding the motorcycle near Ajjapanahalli Gate, Kolar - Mulabagal Road, Kolar Taluk & District and dashed to the rear side of the car that was suddenly took U turn.
This collision resulted in the occurrence of the accident.
The jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and laid charge sheet against driver of car.
9. It is a trite law that a charge sheet is not an conclusive proof to come to the conclusion as to the negligence.
It is a settled principles of law that the tribunal has to assess the documentary and oral evidence and decide the factum of negligence independently.
With this prelude in the backdrop, let me navigate through the oral and documentary proof so as to found out the factum of negligence.
10. Further it is pertinent to note that the petitioners nor the respondents have not examined the eye witness i.e., pillion rider of the motorcycle to prove the said fact.

Further this Court navigate to go on the course of cross examination PW.1, she categorically admitted that they were 4 persons in a motorcycle which was ridden by her husband and the rear portion of car and front portion of motorcycle was damaged.

sentences.text: Further on going through the pleadings the petitioners stated that they were proceeding with motorcycle on the correct side of the road.

On the way when they reached near Ajjapanahalli Gate,
Kolar - Mulabagal NH-75 road, Kolar Taluk and District, one Maruthi Ertiga car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MF-7728 came from same direction, driven by its driver at high speed in rash and negligent manner and while taking a U turn, he lost control over his vehicle, went its wrong side of the road and dashed violently against the deceased's motorcycle from behind.
The pleadings and the cross examination of PW.1 is clinches the facts of the case.
The PW.1 has admitted in her cross examination that rear side of the car portion was damaged and front side of the motorcycle was damaged.
12. Another important document from which a light could be culled out is Ex.P.6 being the IMV Report.
On careful perusal of the same it reflects that the car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MF-7728 was damaged to its rear left side bumper and rear left side body.
This categorically reflect that the impact to the car is from rear side and which in a way spells out that an accident is occurred not due to the negligence of driver of car.

Added more the two wheeler was damaged in the front registration number plate, front left side indicator, right side crash guard, right side rear view mirror, head light visor scratches and this factum also categorically reflect as to the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased also.
13. One of the document which sheds light on the factum of negligence is Ex.P.4 and 5 being the Spot mahazar and spot sketch.
On careful perusal of Ex.P.4 & 5 it reflects that insured vehicle was going from Kolar to Mulabagal on the left side of the service road.

Further the said documents discloses that the car was going on the left side of the road and in order to took U turn near Ajjappanahalli Gate, and the rider of the motorcycle / deceased came from behind of the car and dashed to the car.
When this Court navigates through the contents of Ex.P.4 & 5 it is forthcoming that the said road is high way and the said road is 25 feet in width.
The deceased was going towards Mulabagal from Kolar side.
If the deceased / rider of the two wheeler was coming in a normal speed then he would have certainly avoided the accident.
Another important aspect is to be noted herein the back side of the car was damaged and front side of the deceased motorcycle was damaged.
This categorically reveals that there is also negligence on the part of deceased.
14. Further the claimants have stated that the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the insured vehicle and charge sheet has been filed against the insured vehicle.
But that itself is not enough to distrust the version of the claimants.
The deceased who was coming from the rear side of the car has to look for the vehicular movement on the highway road.
The contents of spot mahazar and spot sketch discloses that the respondent No.2 car driver had a clear vision as it is a straight road.
If the car driver was take some precaution while taking U turn in a normal speed then he would have certainly avoided the accident.
The documents clears that the driver of the car suddenly had taken the U turn from the left side of the motorcycle and suddenly came in front of the motorcycle.
Therefore the rider of the motorcycle dashed to the rear side of the car.
There is a greater amount of negligence on the part of respondent No.2 car driver.
The police records are blatantly and blissfully silent as to the whether there was any negligence on the part of the deceased to avoid the accident.

sentences.text: Further it is also relevant to place reliance on the concept of last opportunity doctrine.
At this juncture it is also relevant to have the concept of doctrine of last opportunity.

The said doctrine is said to have emanated from the principle enunciated in Devies v. Mann (1842 (10) M&W 546) which has often been explained as amounting to a rule that when both parties are careless the party which has the last opportunity of avoiding the results of the other's carelessness is alone liable.
However, according to Lord Denning it is not a principle of law, but test of causation.

(See Davies v.
Swan Motor Co. (Swansea) Ltd. (1949 (2) KB 291).

entities.text:
Davies v.
Swan Motor Co. (Swansea) Ltd. (1949 (2) KB 291
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though in some decisions, the doctrine has been applied by courts, after the decisions of the House of Lords in The Volute (1922 (1) AC 129) and Swadling v. Cooper (1931 AC 1), it is no longer to be applied.
The sample test is what was the cause or what were the causes of the damage.

The act or omission amounting to want of ordinary care or in defiance of duty or obligation on the part of the complaining party which conjointly with the other party's negligence was the proximate cause of the accident renders it one to be the result of contributory negligence.
16. No doubt the driver of the respondent No.2 car had a clear line of vision and could not have missed seeing the deceased motorcycle which was coming from hind side.
But the very act of the respondent No.2 car suddenly took U turn without giving any indications itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
In this view of the matter lesser degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the deceased.
The driver of the respondent No.2 car had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.

The driver of the insured car who had failed to adhere to the basic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner on a highway without observing on going vehicles had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
In this view of the matter lesser degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the deceased.
Hence negligence is fixed on the driver of car & deceased/rider of motorcycle in the ratio of 80 : 20 respectively.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioners claim that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 are the minor children and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief- examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of petitioners are marked at Ex's.P.10 to 14 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the claimants is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the claimants are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, claimants are the legal heir and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that deceased was working as Mason and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this court.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

sentences.text:
Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/-
per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

19. The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P10 wherein the date of deceased is mentioned as 02.11.1992, which indicates that he was aged (31 years 1 months 29 days) 31 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '16'.
20.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 31 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 31 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- i.e. 40%).
21.
The deceased died living behind 4 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.16,800/- p.m. (Rs.22,400 - Rs.5,600 = Rs.16,800/-).
22. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.16,800/- p.m. and the multiplier '16' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.32,25,600/- (Rs.16,800 X 12 X 16).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.32,25,600/- under the head of loss of dependency.

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
24.
In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the minor children and the petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased

and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father, as well as Petitioner no.4 towards deceased her son.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES : 26-Medical bills produced by PW.1 are marked at Ex.P15.

As per that,
the claimants have spent Rs.1,20,371/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.
The said bills have been meticulously examined and is found to be correct.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the genuineness of these bills.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,20,371/- which is rounded off to Rs.1,20,400/- is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
28. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending car are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.28,40,560/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 25%
 Petitioner No.2 - 25%
 Petitioner No.3 - 25%
 Petitioner No.4 - 25%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 & 4

a sum equal to 30% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 70% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to the tremendous impact the deceased fell down along with his motorcycle and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.
On the next day he was shifted to Venkateshwara Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and discharged on 03.01.2024.
On the same day he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, wherein during the course of treatment he succumed the said injuries on 05.01.2024 at about 3.00 p.m.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending car and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Infact the accident occurred due to the sole negligence & reckless driving of the deceased himself he was without maintaining the safe distance between the vehicles and without having proper lookout the vehicular movements of the road in carelessly and in the process he lost control and hit the stationed vehicle from behind and caused the accident.
Further the deceased was riding his motorcycle that too without wearing a helmet and without possessing DL.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 31.12.2023 at about 4.30 p.m.,
near Ajjappanahalli gate U turn, NH-75 road, Kolar - Mulabagal road, Kolar Taluk, Kolar District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of the Maruti Ertiga car bearing Reg.No.KA-53- Shwetha K vs Kartikey Kumar Shukla on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127269412/
3 MF-7728 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ?
If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
9. It is a trite law that a charge sheet is not an conclusive proof to come to the conclusion as to the negligence.
It is a settled principles of law that the tribunal has to assess the documentary and oral evidence and decide the factum of negligence independently.
Shwetha K vs Kartikey Kumar Shukla on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127269412/
4 11.
There is a greater amount of negligence on the part of respondent No.2 car driver.
The police records are blatantly and blissfully silent as to the whether there was any negligence on the part of the deceased to avoid the accident.
Shwetha K vs Kartikey Kumar Shukla on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127269412/
5 15.
(See Davies v.
Swan Motor Co. (Swansea) Ltd. (1949 (2) KB 291).
The act or omission amounting to want of ordinary care or in defiance of duty or obligation on the part of the complaining party which conjointly with the other party's negligence was the proximate cause of the accident renders it one to be the result of contributory negligence.
But the very act of the respondent No.2 car suddenly took U turn without giving any indications itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
In this view of the matter lesser degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the deceased.
The driver of the respondent No.2 car had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
The driver of the insured car who had failed to adhere to the basic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner on a highway without observing on going vehicles had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
In this view of the matter lesser degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the deceased.
Hence negligence is fixed on the driver of car & deceased/rider of motorcycle in the ratio of 80 : 20 respectively.
Since the evidence led by the claimants is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the claimants are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, claimants are the legal heir and dependents of deceased.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Shwetha K vs Kartikey Kumar Shukla on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127269412/
6
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 31 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.
and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father, as well as Petitioner no.4 towards deceased her son.
opennyai_summary.decision:
22. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.16,800/- p.m. and the multiplier '16' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.32,25,600/- (Rs.16,800 X 12 X 16).
Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.32,25,600/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,20,371/- which is rounded off to Rs.1,20,400/- is awarded under this head.
26. The calculation table stands as follows :
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.32,25,600/-
 2. Towards loss of Consortium to Rs. 48,400/-
 the petitioner No.1  3. Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150/-
Medical Expenses Rs. 1,20,400/-
 Total Rs.35,50,700/-
 Less 20% towards contributory Rs. 7,10,140/-
 negligence on the part of the  deceased  (Rs.35,50,700 - 7,10,140)
28. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending car are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.28,40,560/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 25%
 Petitioner No.2 - 25%
 Petitioner No.3 - 25%
 Petitioner No.4 - 25%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 & 4
a sum equal to 30% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 70% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
